chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Sabbah ibn Sayaba, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so Muhammad ibn 'Abdah said to him, 'Does the adulterer commit adultery while he is a believer?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No. When he is upon her belly, faith is stripped from him. So when he arises, it is returned to him.' I said, 'Supposing he intends to return?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'How often do they consider returning, then they do not return.'
ai.seo_question: Does a person lose their faith completely during the act of adultery according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of 'temporary loss of faith' (firqan al-iman) during the actual performance of major sins, distinguishing it from permanent apostasy. It highlights the nuanced Shia view that while the adulterer remains a believer in essence, the specific act of zina suspends the manifestation of iman until completion, though the narrator's observation warns that habitual sinners often fail to truly repent. This aligns with the broader theological discourse on the relationship between action and belief in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, from Sabbah Bin Sayaba who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, so Muhammad Bin Abdat said to himasws, ‘Would the adulterer commit adultery while he is a Momin?’ Heasws said: ‘No. When he was upon her belly, the Emān was Confiscated from him. So when he arose, it was returned to him’. I said, ‘Supposing he intends to return?’ Heasws said: ‘How often do they consider returning then they do not return’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from Sabah ibn Siyabah who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and Muhammad ibn ‘Abdahu said, ‘A fornicator fornicates. Is he still a believer?’ The Imam said, ‘As long as he is on her belly he is not a believer and when he stands up, belief is returned to him.’ I then asked, ‘What if one intends to repeat?’ The Imam said, ‘How many are they who intend but do not repeat!”’
